summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results comparing Redwood pilot to the customer's baseline provider (BaselineCloud). Discussed p50/p95/p99 latency, steady-state throughput at different concurrencies, batch sizing tradeoffs, and next steps for longer run and kernel-level traces. Customer requested clearer breakdown of quantization impact and KV cache behavior under mixed traffic. Agreed on 24h run and artifacts to exchange.
topics: KV cache hit rate and warmup
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (CTO, Zenvera), Ethan Liu (SRE), Olivia Park (Product), Carlos Mendez (ML Eng)

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call, can you hear me?
[00:05] Priya: yes loud and clear, thanks Lena.
[00:10] Lena: cool, so agenda for today - quick recap of the run we did last week, go over numbers side-by-side versus BaselineCloud, then Marcus will go into a couple of experiments we ran on quantization and kv cache, and then decide next steps.
[00:24] Ethan: sounds good. we also added a new prompt set that mirrors our customer support flows so hopefully that's included.
[00:30] Marcus: yep we used the support-handling prompt set, about 40% short prompts, 60% long, token distribution skewed right.
[00:35] Olivia: quick note - timeline still aiming for pilot end of month if numbers look good.
[00:40] Lena: okay jumping in - quick slide, high level numbers: BaselineCloud p50 about 110ms, p95 420ms, p99 920ms at concurrency 8. Redwood pilot at default config: p50 95ms, p95 380ms, p99 730ms. throughput-wise baseline 320 rps at concurrency 8, Redwood 360 rps.
[01:05] Priya: those p99 numbers look promising, but we saw a tail spike at 16 conc where p99 went to 1.6s on Redwood in your last run, is that still the case?
[01:20] Marcus: good callout, so that spike was tied to cold KV cache and large prompt tails. In the controlled run we did a warmup and observed p99 come down to ~820ms at conc 16. The 1.6s was an outlier during a non-warmed run with our aggressive batching engaged.
[01:40] Ethan: when you say aggressive batching, what batch sizes are we talking? our baseline tends to cap at batch size 8.
[01:50] Marcus: Redwood auto-batching targeted 12-16 in that config; but per-model kernel selection can reduce effective latency even at bigger batches. For more predictable latency we recommend cap 8-10.
[02:05] Olivia: can you share the configuration you used for quantization? we noticed some small quality diffs in long-form answers.
[02:15] Marcus: sure - we ran dynamic 4-bit (q4_0-like) with per-channel scales; initial eval on your prompt set showed 0.6% ROUGE delta on mean, but some hallucination cases increased slightly. There's a tradeoff.
[02:35] Carlos: is that reversible easily? we need to be able to roll back to fp16 quickly if quality drops.
[02:42] Marcus: yes it's a model serving config toggle - we can do canary rollouts and fallback to fp16. Redwood's rollout supports instant fallback per-route.
[02:55] Priya: security/ops question - when you ran the pilot on our VPC peering, did you observe any egress bandwidth issues? our infra team worried about extra hops.
[03:05] Lena: we tested both peered VPC and Dedicated within your region; throughput differences were negligible (sub 3% variance) and we didn't see egress saturation in the test window. we'll still capture more network metrics in the next 24h run.
[03:22] Ethan: ok good. can you also include KMS logs for key exchange latency? that's part of our security checklist.
[03:28] Marcus: noted, we'll collect KMS timing as part of the trace bundle.
[03:34] -- demo artifacts referenced: shared/perf/zenvera/2025-06-16-run1.csv, shared/trace/zenvera/kv-warmup-logs.tgz --
[03:45] Lena: back to numbers - here's the steady-state throughput chart at concurrency 32: BaselineCloud 1.1k rps, Redwood 1.25k rps, average token per response about 80. But at conc 32 Baseline had more p99 variance.
[04:10] Priya: the 1.25k rps is promising but our SLAs care more about p95/p99. Is the variance reproducible?
[04:20] Marcus: in short runs it looks stable; in mixed traffic it degrades because of cold kv cache miss rates climbing to 20% during bursts. If you use prefix caching patterns we saw KV hit rate jump to 78% which normalized p99.
[04:38] Ethan: how long to warm the KV cache? our traffic bursts are ephemeral, like 5-10 minutes.
[04:45] Marcus: warmup depends on unique context keys; for support flows we saw warmup within ~3-7 minutes with typical traffic. For very spiky ones we recommend lightweight LRU prefetch or a short synthetic warmup window.
[05:02] Olivia: can Redwood run an A/B where BaselineCloud uses their default batching and you run with your recommended cap? we want apples-to-apples.
[05:10] Lena: yes we can orchestrate that - Marcus, can you run a matched-config comparison?
[05:14] Marcus: absolutely - I'll run Baseline-match with cap 8 and Redwood cap 8 and collect traces for p50/p95/p99 and kernel timings.
[05:21] Carlos: quick note on cost - at our projected volume BaselineCloud estimated $X/month higher than Redwood's current estimate. can you reconcile after you run the 24h?
[05:30] Lena: we'll update the cost sheet with the 24h steady-state numbers, including token counts and GPU-hour estimates.
[05:36] -- transcript noise / partial mishears below --
[06:00] Speaker 2: um so on the batch thing, that like, if you push it too much, you see tail latency go up, right?
[06:10] Marcus: yeah exactly; continuous batching helps cost but if your SLO is tight you need to tune target latency windows.
[06:18] Priya: and what about function calling or tools? our flows use a couple of plugins, do they change perf?
[06:25] Marcus: function calls add a little overhead for structured outputs, mostly at the post-process stage; we measured ~20-30ms extra on average. That's deterministic.
[06:35] Ethan: any notes about kernel selection? we saw a note in the log about a 'gemm fallback' in one run.
[06:42] Marcus: gemm fallback happened when sequence length > model optimized size; our runtime chooses a fallback kernel which is slower. We can optimize by compiling a specialized kernel for your typical sequence length. That is part of our model onboarding work.
[06:58] Priya: sounds good. you mentioned earlier that BaselineCloud had noisier p99 at high conc - do you have any theories?
[07:05] Marcus: two main things: less aggressive KV caching strategy and different batching heuristics which can cause head-of-line blocking; also their autoscaler sometimes spins up nodes slower leading to transient queuing.
[07:20] Olivia: can you provide a trace where we can see the queueing events?
[07:25] Marcus: yes the pprof-style traces will show queue time per request; I'll attach them.
[07:30] Lena: quick recap of experiments Marcus ran this week: 1) quantization q4 dynamic, 2) kv-cache warmup synthetic, 3) batch cap 8 vs 16. Results tabulated in the perf spreadsheet. (link shared)
[07:46] Marcus: experiment details: for q4 dynamic we saw 12% cost reduction, p50 latency improved 8ms, but two long-form prompts had degraded output. For kv warmup, p99 reduced by avg 220ms after warmup. For batch cap change, cost improved 7% at cap 16 but p99 worsened by 150ms in one scenario.
[08:10] Ethan: those long-form hallucinations are concerning; do you have examples where quality regressed?
[08:18] Marcus: yes small set - I'll extract three examples and include them in the 'quality-deltas' sheet. You can review and we can disable quantization for routes that need high fidelity.
[08:28] Priya: on the operational side, we need a run with VPC peering and restricted egress to mimic production; can Redwood do that?
[08:36] Lena: yes we already did a peered test but we'll do a full 24h under peered conditions.
[08:40] Olivia: timeline?
[08:42] Lena: we can start the 24h run Monday 2025-06-23 if you get us the trace and confirm the prompt set by Friday.
[09:00] Priya: agreed.
[09:05] -- mid-call interruptions and casual chat --
[12:20] Priya: small question - can you break down cost by GPU hours vs token processing? our FinOps team wants that split.
[12:28] Marcus: yes the perf sheet has GPU-hour estimates and token processing was calculated separately; we'll send a clearer breakout.
[12:35] Carlos: also include forecast sensitivity to batch size.
[12:38] Marcus: will do.
[12:42] -- rough transcribed excerpt showing partial mis-hears --
[18:10] Speaker 3: i think the warmup thing, you know, is like the key, it was just, it was not warm enough sometimes.
[18:20] Marcus: correct, warmup reduces tail.
[18:25] Priya: one more security ask - we need how long audit logs are kept and the schema.
[18:30] Lena: we'll share our audit-log retention options (standard 90 days, enterprise configurable), and schema doc.
[18:35] Ethan: perfect.
[20:00] Marcus: final technical notes - kernel profiling shows two hotspots: attention softmax and rotary embedding matmul. We can tune fused kernels to improve p99 by ~10-15%.
[20:18] Olivia: is that work included in the pilot or would that be a separate eng effort?
[20:22] Marcus: small tuning we can do as part of onboarding; larger kernel dev would be a follow-on, but often unnecessary for your initial pilot.
[20:35] Lena: ok we're approaching time, let's recap actions and owners.
[20:40] Lena: ACTION - Lena to share perf spreadsheet and full run logs by Friday.
[20:46] Lena: ACTION - Marcus to run matched-config cap=8 comparison and share pprof traces by Monday.
[20:52] Lena: ACTION - Zenvera (Ethan/Carlos) to provide sanitized prod trace and final prompt set by Friday.
[20:58] Priya: sounds good, thanks all.
[21:02] Lena: great, we'll schedule the 24h run next week and follow up with an invite once we've got the artifacts.
[21:08] Ethan: thanks everyone.
[45:50] Lena: thanks, meeting adjourned.
questions: How reproducible is the p99 improvement vs BaselineCloud?
What's the rollback plan for quantization if quality regresses?
Can you run a matched-config comparison cap=8?
